svg.title: Text start and text rules
svg.desc: The text start behind both metadata blocks with its three articles, each in stream order with real excerpts of the dictionary article, the contributor names and the census template texts. Dashed boxes mark bytes that are fed to the models and not coded. They are the head line in front of each article, the day of the revision, the mark and a tab in front of each contributor line, and the word codes in front of the dictionary article and the word stems behind it, both fed to PPMd only. Below are the three reversible text rules a/an, title and link, each with a real line of enwik9 and the same line in the coder stream.
svg.text: Text start and reversible text rules
Both change the stream form. The decoder restores the original bytes.
not to scale; the text start is the first text
fed to the models, not coded
The dictionary itself, one word per line
in code order; the decoder rebuilds the
dictionary from it. A word of more than 7
letters starts with the code of its longest
earlier prefix of 7 letters or more; an empty
line marks where the order starts again.
The names of part B of the metadata block,
one line per record with a name mark, in
the order of part B. In front of each line
all models are fed the day of its revision,
its mark (05 new name, 03 repeated name)
The template texts of the census form,
each variant once, and the words of the
states and place types. The census records
PPMd only: the codes of all 54,857 words
woul ther wer hav ofte onl ...
88 BD in base 100 is day 861, counted
from 1 Jan 2001 in months of 31 days.

text.tspan: Reversible text rules on the page text
titles and links shorten the stream by 4,880,702 B; a/an keeps its length

svg.text: the article is written as the code of a where a fixed
rule on the next word (with 44 listed exceptions)
gives the right article, else as the code of an
to destabilize an authority ... against an unpopular
to destabilize a authority ... against a unpopular
the first bold text, an interwiki title or a category
sort key that equals the page title (or one of
its forms) is left empty; 0x01 bytes select the form
a link text that follows from the link target (for
example the target without its bracket part)
is left empty; 0x01 bytes select the form
Stream lines show dictionary codes as words; single brackets come from the preprocessing that 1.0 already had.
